official.deadline_note: All application materials are due 1 October 2027 except the three letters of recommendation, which are due 8 October 2027. Once submitted, no changes can be made by either the applicant or the NHC.
official.application_cycle: Applications for the 2028-29 academic year open on 1 July 2027 and close on 1 October 2027
official.status_note: The competition runs each year from 1 July to early October. The 1 October 2026 deadline has passed, so the current cycle is closed; the Center states it will begin accepting applications for the 2028-29 academic year on 1 July 2027 with a deadline of 1 October 2027.
benefits: Individually determined stipend; the Center seeks to provide half salary with the expectation that the Fellow's home institution covers the remaining salary.
Round-trip travel to Durham, North Carolina and back for the Fellow and immediate family living with the Fellow.
Access to the Center's library and reference support, dining services and intellectual community.
Fellows who come from overseas are provided with guidance on housing, local transportation and finding schools.
eligibility: The applicant holds a PhD or relevant terminal degree for their primary discipline (for example an MFA for research-based non-fiction writers).

The PhD or requisite terminal degree was received at least five years prior to 1 October 2027, that is no later than 30 September 2022; or the applicant meets the requirements for the Geiss-Hsu or Philip L. Quinn fellowships.
The applicant has published at least one scholarly monograph, for book-focused fields, or the equivalent in peer-reviewed scholarship for article-focused fields.
The applicant is working on a project beyond the dissertation that is at an advanced stage, meaning that most of the research is done and the applicant is already writing.
The applicant plans to spend the full term, one or two semesters, in residence at the Center; extended time away including trips for field research is not permitted.
The applicant speaks and reads English fluently; it is not required that the primary project publication be written in English.
requirements: A 1,000-word project proposal, in 11 or 12-point font with margins no smaller than one inch.
A short bibliography, two pages maximum, on the same formatting rules.
A brief curriculum vitae, four pages maximum; reviewers may rank a project lower when a longer, less-focused CV is provided.
A one-page tentative outline of the structure of the project, noting the current or projected completion stage for primary components.
Three letters of recommendation, due 8 October 2027, uploaded by the referees through an email prompt.
documents: Project proposal, 1,000 words maximum, noting the current stage of the project and the projected timeline to completion.
Tentative outline of the project, one page maximum.
selection_criteria: NHC Fellows are chosen based not on their record of past achievements but on the strength of the project proposal and its supporting documents.
Clarity of disciplinary and subject-specific knowledge while remaining clear to an interdisciplinary audience.
Evidence of preparedness to complete the project, and explicit treatment of project status and projected timeline - proposals that do not address these are deemed ineligible.
coverage: Individually determined stipend; the Center seeks to provide half salary with the expectation that the Fellow's home institution covers the remaining salary.
Round-trip travel expenses for the Fellow and those family members who will live with the Fellow during their time in North Carolina.
Stipends are taxable and are salary replacement only; no indirect costs or fringe benefits are included and institutional overhead is not allowed.
application_method: Complete the online application on the Center's application portal.
Upload the proposal, bibliography, CV and outline.
Provide names and contact information for three references, who are emailed a link to upload their letters.
official.application_route: Online application through the Center's portal, with the four documents uploaded by 1 October and the three reference letters uploaded by 8 October.
official.study_mode: Full-time residential: the applicant plans to spend the full term in residence at the Center, and extended time away including field research is not permitted.
official.international_eligibility: The Center has no citizenship requirements and warmly invites international applicants; the Center sponsors J-1 Research Scholar visa applications for Fellows who are not US citizens and can also provide J-2 visas for spouses and children.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The project must be grounded in one or more humanities disciplines, or in other fields but substantially employing humanistic approaches and methodologies. The Center does not fund post-docs, doctoral research, creative writing such as fiction or poetry, edited volumes, collections of primary sources, textbooks or projects derivative of a dissertation.
official.research_requirement: A substantial humanistic scholarly project at an advanced stage, with most of the research complete and writing already begun, that will result in publication. Most projects are single-author scholarly monographs.
official.duration: Academic year (September to May), or fall semester (September to December) or spring semester (January to May).
official.description: The National Humanities Center is a private, nonprofit organization and the only independent institute dedicated exclusively to advanced study in all areas of the humanities. Its Residential Fellowship offers scholars the time, space and support to pursue their work and the opportunity to take part in the Center's intellectual community.
official.program_type: Independent humanities institute research fellowship (private nonprofit)
official.english_requirement: Fluency in written and spoken English is required; it is not required that the primary project publication be written in English.

applicant_utility.summary: This fellowship is won or lost on the proposal, not on your CV - the Center says explicitly that fellows are chosen on the strength of the project and its supporting documents rather than past achievements. Your project must already be well into the writing stage, with most of the research done, and you must say so in the proposal: proposals that do not address project status and projected timeline are deemed ineligible. It is also a half-salary salary-replacement award, not full funding, and you must be physically resident in Durham for the whole term, so field-work-heavy projects are a poor match. Applications for the 2028-29 year open on 1 July 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career and senior humanities scholars with a published monograph or substantial peer-reviewed record and a book project already in draft who can spend a full semester or year in residence.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the five-year clock: your terminal degree must have been awarded no later than 30 September 2022 for the 2028-29 cycle, unless you qualify for the Geiss-Hsu or Quinn fellowships.

Confirm the project is beyond the dissertation, is humanities-grounded, is not creative writing, an edited volume, a primary-source collection or a textbook, and is at an advanced stage with most research complete before you invest in an application.
Draft the 1,000-word proposal so its final paragraph states plainly how much research is done and what you intend to accomplish at the Center.
Cut the CV to four pages focusing on the publication record that positions you for this specific project.
Choose referees who know your work well rather than famous names, and ideally at least one who is outside your own institution.
Confirm you can be continuously in residence in Durham for the full term you request.
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that does not explicitly address project status and projected timeline - the Center deems such proposals ineligible.
A project still in the research phase rather than in the writing phase.
A dissertation derivative, an edited volume, a primary-source collection, a textbook, or fiction or poetry.
A CV longer than four pages, which reviewers may rank lower.
A bibliography over two pages or an outline over one page.
Assuming part-time or remote residence is possible - extended absence including field research is not permitted.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is salary replacement only, and the Center seeks to provide about half of it, so your home institution is expected to cover the remaining salary. No indirect costs, fringe benefits or institutional overhead are included, and the stipend is taxable.
document_audit: The proposal has a hard 1,000-word cap and specific formatting rules: 11 or 12-point font with margins no smaller than one inch.
The tentative outline must note the current or projected completion stage for each primary component - projects not indicating stage of completion are deemed ineligible.
Bibliography is capped at two pages, CV at four pages and the outline at one page; overshooting any of them signals poor self-editing.
Reference letters are uploaded by the referees through an emailed link, so brief them early and confirm they received the prompt.
alerts: Applications for 2028-29 open on 1 July 2027, close 1 October 2027, with letters due 8 October 2027; the 1 October 2026 deadline has already passed.
Once submitted, changes can no longer be made by either the applicant or the NHC, so treat submission as final.

Applicants are informed by email in February, the class is typically announced in early April, and all applicants receive final notification by the end of March; alternates are offered fellowships by telephone.

Dedicated streams exist for HBCU faculty, scholars of Ming-era China, early-career female philosophers and at-risk or refugee scholars - some require a separate route, for example the UNCF/Mellon Program, while others are assessed through the general pool.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You complete the online application on the Center's portal, upload the proposal, bibliography, CV and outline by 1 October, your three referees upload their letters by 8 October, and the Center notifies applicants by email in February with the class announced in early April.
